title: Inkling 2 Small Pricing: API Rates and Limits 2026
summary: Inkling 2 Small pricing goes beyond the sticker price—costs are based on your plan's limits and token rates. Calculate your actual costs for your workload.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Is there a free plan for Inkling 2 Small? We haven't confirmed one, so don't build a budget on the assumption.


Read the vendor's pricing page for any free allowance. If one exists, treat it as a trial for testing your real workload, because a free tier that runs out mid-project costs more than a paid plan chosen up front.


Does Inkling 2 Small charge extra for long context? We couldn't confirm a long-context surcharge, and that's exactly why you should check.


Long documents mean more tokens per request, and on usage-based billing every request costs more even without a surcharge. Look at the vendor's API pricing page for any separate rate on large inputs, then run one typical long document through and read the bill.


### Can I cancel or downgrade mid-billing-cycle?


Whether you get a refund or credit for the unused time is a billing-terms question, and we have no confirmed answer. Before you commit, read the vendor's terms for cancellation and plan changes.


If a downgrade only takes effect at renewal, you pay the higher rate until then, so time the change for just before renewal rather than just after.


Is there a discount for annual billing or nonprofits? We have no confirmed discount to report.


Annual prepayment often trades a lower rate for less flexibility, and if the plan turns out to be too small or too big, you're locked in.


Ask the vendor's sales or support channel in writing, and ask the nonprofit question directly rather than waiting for a banner on the pricing page.


### What happens when you hit the usage limit?


We won't guess at this, because the vendor's usage documentation is the only authority. The outcome is usually one of three: you're throttled, you're blocked until the limit resets, or you're billed overage.


Each costs you differently, and blocking in the middle of a working day is often the most expensive of the three. Find out which one applies before you depend on the plan, not after the first interrupted job.
